questions.question: In a flow network, an original edge $i\to j$ has capacity $c_{ij}$ and carries a feasible flow $x_{ij}$ with $0\le x_{ij}\le c_{ij}$. What are its residual capacities in the forward direction $i\to j$ and in the reverse direction $j\to i$?
options: $c_{ij}-x_{ij}$ forward and $x_{ij}$ reverse
$x_{ij}$ forward and $c_{ij}-x_{ij}$ reverse
$c_{ij}$ forward and $c_{ij}$ reverse
$c_{ij}-x_{ij}$ forward and $0$ reverse

questions.question: In a flow network, an original edge $i\to j$ has capacity $c_{ij}$ and carries a feasible flow $x_{ij}$ with $0\le x_{ij}\le c_{ij}$. In the residual network there is a reverse direction $j\to i$ with residual capacity $x_{ij}>0$. What does using this reverse direction mean?
options: Sending new flow along a road from $j$ to $i$.
Cancelling part of the flow already assigned to $i\to j$.
Treating the edge as undirected, with capacity $c_{ij}$ both ways.
Using the capacity of an original edge $j\to i$.

questions.question: An edge $i\to j$ of a flow network has capacity $c_{ij}>0$ and is saturated: its flow $x_{ij}$ equals $c_{ij}$. Writing residual capacities as (forward, reverse), which pair does the edge have?
In a flow network, edge $i\to j$ has capacity $c_{ij}>0$ but currently carries flow $x_{ij}=0$. Writing residual capacities as (forward, reverse), what pair belongs to this empty edge?

In a flow network, an original edge $i\to j$ has capacity $c_{ij}$ and carries a feasible flow $x_{ij}$ with $0\le x_{ij}\le c_{ij}$. In a drawing of the residual network, the connection between $i$ and $j$ carries two labels, 4 towards $j$ and 2 towards $i$. How should the two labels be read?
options: Up to 4 more units $i\to j$; up to 2 units can be cancelled.
The connection can carry 4 units in each direction.
Up to 6 units can move between $i$ and $j$ either way.
The connection carries 3 units on average in each direction.

questions.question: In a flow network, an original edge $i\to j$ has capacity $c_{ij}$ and carries a feasible flow $x_{ij}$ with $0\le x_{ij}\le c_{ij}$. Answers are written as (forward residual capacity, reverse residual capacity). For $c_{ij}=9$ and $x_{ij}=4$, what are the residual capacities?

In a flow network, an original edge $i\to j$ has capacity $c_{ij}$ and carries a feasible flow $x_{ij}$ with $0\le x_{ij}\le c_{ij}$. Answers are written as (forward residual capacity, reverse residual capacity). With $c_{ij}=9$ and $x_{ij}=4$, the flow on $i\to j$ is raised by 2 units. What are the new residual capacities?

In a flow network, an original edge $i\to j$ has capacity $c_{ij}$ and carries a feasible flow $x_{ij}$ with $0\le x_{ij}\le c_{ij}$. Answers are written as (forward residual capacity, reverse residual capacity). With $c_{ij}=7$ and $x_{ij}=5$, three units of the flow on $i\to j$ are cancelled. What are the new residual capacities?

In a flow network, an original edge $i\to j$ has capacity $c_{ij}$ and carries a feasible flow $x_{ij}$ with $0\le x_{ij}\le c_{ij}$. In the residual network the edge shows forward residual capacity 2 and reverse residual capacity 5. What is its capacity $c_{ij}$?
A flow network has edges $S\to A$ (capacity 4, flow 4), $A\to T$ (capacity 5, flow 4) and $S\to T$ (capacity 3, flow 0). Which directions have positive residual capacity?
options: $A\to T$ (1) and $S\to T$ (3) only

questions.question: In a maximum flow problem, the residual network records, for each edge, how much flow could be added and how much could be cancelled. Why are the reverse (cancelling) directions needed?
options: They are only a drawing convention and carry no information.
They let flows become negative on edges that are full.
They enlarge the capacity of edges already in use.
Good routings may need part of an earlier choice undone.

questions.question: For a flow network, the residual network is built for the zero flow ($x_{ij}=0$ on every edge). How does it compare with the original network?
options: Every edge appears forward and in reverse, each direction with capacity $c_{ij}$.
It has the original edges with their capacities, and no reverse ones.
It has no edges at all, since residual edges only arise once flow is sent.
Every edge appears only in the reverse direction, with capacity $c_{ij}$.

questions.question: In a flow network, an original edge $i\to j$ has capacity $c_{ij}$ and carries a feasible flow $x_{ij}$ with $0\le x_{ij}\le c_{ij}$. A student computes the forward residual of an edge as $c_{ij}-x_{ij}=5-7=-2$. What does this reveal?
options: The flow is infeasible, since $x_{ij}=7$ exceeds $c_{ij}=5$.
The edge can still take 2 units in the reverse direction.
The value should be read as 0, so the edge is just saturated.
The reverse residual is $7+2=9$ units of cancellable flow.

questions.question: A flow network has edges $S\to A$ (capacity 6, flow 2) and $A\to T$ (capacity 4, flow 3). The flow on both edges is raised by 1.  Answers are written as (forward residual capacity, reverse residual capacity). What are the new residual capacities of $S\to A$ and of $A\to T$?

In a flow network, an original edge $i\to j$ has capacity $c_{ij}$ and carries a feasible flow $x_{ij}$ with $0\le x_{ij}\le c_{ij}$. With $c_{ij}=8$ and $x_{ij}=5$, by how many units can the flow on $i\to j$ at most be reduced?

In a residual network, each original edge shows (forward, reverse) residual capacities: $A\to B$ $(0,6)$, $A\to C$ $(2,3)$, $B\to D$ $(0,4)$, $C\to D$ $(5,0)$. Which original edges are saturated, that is, carry flow equal to their capacity?
options: $C\to D$ only
$A\to B$ and $B\to D$
$A\to B$ only
$A\to C$ and $C\to D$

questions.question: In a flow network, an original edge $i\to j$ has capacity $c_{ij}$ and carries a feasible flow $x_{ij}$ with $0\le x_{ij}\le c_{ij}$. Why is the reverse residual capacity $x_{ij}$ and not $c_{ij}$?
options: It should be $c_{ij}$, as the edge could carry $c_{ij}$ units back.
It should be $c_{ij}-x_{ij}$, the room left on the edge.
Only assigned flow can be cancelled, as flows stay nonnegative.
It has no fixed limit, since cancelling never breaks a constraint.

questions.question: In a flow network, an original edge $i\to j$ has capacity $c_{ij}$ and carries a feasible flow $x_{ij}$ with $0\le x_{ij}\le c_{ij}$. When do both residual directions of the edge have positive capacity?
options: Exactly when $x_{ij}>0$.
Exactly when $x_{ij}<c_{ij}$.
Exactly when $0<x_{ij}<c_{ij}$.
Always, for every edge with $c_{ij}>0$.

questions.question: A flow from source $S$ to sink $T$ has residual (forward, reverse) capacities $S\to A$ $(1,3)$, $S\to B$ $(0,2)$, $A\to T$ $(2,3)$ and $B\to T$ $(4,2)$ on its four original edges. What is the value of the flow?
A path $S\to A\to T$ is the whole of a flow network. A student reports residual (forward, reverse) capacities $(2,3)$ on $S\to A$ and $(1,4)$ on $A\to T$. Can these come from a feasible flow?
options: No; they give 3 units into $A$ but 4 out of $A$.
Yes; all residual capacities are nonnegative.
No; the capacity of $S\to A$ would then be exceeded.
Yes, since conservation is not needed at $A$.
